items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1970-11-14
items.q: The kid Rene, what do you remember? On Court Street. I never know him to live anywhere else myself, you know.

ctx.x: Mike, when you were playing up, do you consider the best cornet player?

Oh, that's a kind of hard thing. Sure. To say, because you know the reason why, when I was a kid, you're talking about it? Yeah. Because I was listening to the cornet and trumpets all my, what's that cornet then, that damn night. All my days, I just loved it. My mother wouldn't buy me one. She wouldn't buy me a violin. I didn't want to buy me. But anyway, I had my, well, before Ludd, John Tron came along, I was crazy about my teacher, Manuel Perez. He had such a name around there, you know, around him. He, when…
I said, plenty gold on the lawn socks. No, I didn't know.

items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: Yeah he played there on Lincoln Park. I met him later in later years

ctx.x: So I went with the old man I think a little over two years. He was living right there on the man in St. Claude, not very far from him. And we used to pay 25 cents for a lesson. 25 cents for a lesson at the time. And that was, well that was up around 29 I imagine. Yeah. And a portion of 30, about 29 anyhow. Yeah that's right. So I got a job at Tucky Hall on the last of 29. That was my first regular job. That was the fine dance hall. I took a band in there. We worked about two and a half years over there.
I remember I was there when Kid Nene was playing, we were on the play there on Lincoln Park.

Yeah he played there on Lincoln Park. I met him later in later years I went back and worked there when it was Budweiser then. You see I went there and worked later on. I think around 37 or something. With Butler Rap, he had the band over there at the time. That was around 37.
